about: the path and confounder claims of Knowledge: the exactness lanes and, on simulated data, each method with true claims against the same fit without them
build: Andrey pre-release build of 9 November 2026 on the 0.16.0 release branch (version string 0.16.0)
verdict_rule: per method, cell, part, and fraction: D = errors(with true claims) - errors(without) per dataset, seeds 0-19; worse when the 95% percentile-bootstrap interval of mean D lies above 0, better when below; a worse row counts only when the same row on seeds 100-119 is worse too in the same measure. The cpdag lane judges two measures, errors and dag_errors (dag_* fields), and a row worse again in either counts. Floor: the interval of errors - empty-graph errors must lie below 0. A row with in_setting false lies outside the method's stated setting (ges at expected degree 4) and is reported, not judged. A part of a method passes when no judged row is worse again, every judged row is below the floor, and its exactness lane has no failure.
error_metric: pag, lpcmci, lingam: pairs adjacent in the fit and not in the truth, or the reverse, plus every tail or arrowhead, on a pair adjacent in both, that differs from the true MAG of the observed variables (pag), the true window MAG (lpcmci), or the true DAG (lingam); a circle is never wrong. cpdag: errors is the structural Hamming distance (andrey.metrics.shd) to the class the truth and the fit's true claims define, the true CPDAG without claims and the MPDAG of the true class under the claims with them; dag_errors is the endpoint-aware distance to the true DAG (an edge directed as the DAG directs it 0, an undirected edge 1, a reversed, missing, or extra edge 2); reversed_with and reversed_without are the mean numbers of edges directed against the true DAG; edges_directed_by_claims counts, on pairs adjacent in the truth, the edges directed with the claims beyond those directed without, and of_them_against_the_true_dag those directed against the true DAG
dropped_note: claims is the number of true claims given to the fits of a row and dropped the number the fits dropped as unmet by the graph they found; knowledge_error counts fits that raised
no_dataset_note: seeds whose graph has too few nodes with two children to hide the cell's hidden nodes; left out of the pag lane
false_claims_note: rows with arm false state 10% of the ordered pairs wrongly: context, not judged
against_lingam_note: D = errors(direct_lingam) - errors(lingam's DirectLiNGAM with the same claims as prior_knowledge) on the datasets both fit; part none is the fit without claims; lingam_failed counts the datasets where lingam raised

wrong_directions.about: the single-part fits of the cpdag lane on seeds 0-19 and 100-119, refit keeping each graph: on pairs adjacent in the truth, the edges directed with the claims and undirected without, by whether the graph found without claims stands for the true DAG

classes.holds_true_dag: the true DAG is one of the DAGs the graph found stands for
classes.adjacency_differs: an edge is missing or extra
classes.collider_differs: the adjacencies are the truth's and a collider is not

references.about: each method against reference packages given the same knowledge, on the datasets of the lanes above; seeds 0-19, worse rows repeated on seeds 100-119

packages.tetrad.pc: Tetrad 7.6.10 PC, Fisher z at alpha 0.05, required and forbidden edges as Knowledge
packages.tetrad.ges: Tetrad 7.6.10 FGES, SEM BIC with penalty discount 1 (the plain BIC), three passes of forward and backward search, Knowledge
packages.tetrad.boss: Tetrad 7.6.10 BOSS, SEM BIC with penalty discount 1, Knowledge
packages.tetrad.fci: Tetrad 7.6.10 FCI, Fisher z at alpha 0.05, Knowledge, excludeSelectionBias=true in both arms
packages.tetrad.boss_fci: Tetrad 7.6.10 BOSS-FCI, Knowledge, excludeSelectionBias=true in both arms
packages.tetrad.gfci: GFCI of causal-cmd 1.12.0, which bundles tetrad-lib 7.6.3, Knowledge
packages.pcalg.pc: pcalg pc, Gaussian test at alpha 0.05; required pairs kept adjacent with fixedEdges, then each required and forbidden edge applied with addBgKnowledge one at a time, an edge it refuses left out
packages.tigramite.lpcmci: tigramite 5.2.10.1 LPCMCI, ParCorr at pc_alpha 0.05, the claims as link_assumptions
packages.lingam.direct_lingam: lingam DirectLiNGAM, the claims as prior_knowledge

references.translation: the references of the cpdag and pag lanes take edges, not paths: a forbidden path a -> b becomes the forbidden edge a -> b; a required path on a pair adjacent in the true graph becomes the required edge a -> b; a required path on any other pair, and a confounded pair, has no edge form and is left out. A required edge says more than the path it comes from: it states that the pair is adjacent.
references.arms: same_edges: the method with the translated edges as required and forbidden against the reference with the same edges. same_claims: the method with the claims against a reference that takes the claims themselves (tigramite, lingam). claims_against_reference: the method with the path claims against the reference with the translated edges. without_knowledge: both without knowledge. ges_bic is ges with ebic_gamma=0, the plain BIC of the FGES arm.
references.rule: per method, reference, cell, part, and fraction: D = errors(method) - errors(reference) per dataset both fit, dag_errors in cpdag and errors elsewhere; worse when the 95% percentile-bootstrap interval of mean D (10,000 resamples) lies above 0; a worse row counts when the same row on seeds 100-119 is worse too. Floor: the interval of the method's errors minus the empty graph's must lie below 0. Rows with in_setting false (ges at expected degree 4) are reported and not judged. A part of a method is supported when it passes the lanes above and, with the same knowledge as the reference (same_edges or same_claims), no judged row of its own, or of the all-parts runs for required_paths, is worse again against a reference or misses the floor. claims_against_reference is not like for like and does not decide the status: the reference's required edge also states that the pair is adjacent, which the translation reads from the true graph, and a path claim does not. status lists its rows that are worse again under path_claims_against_reference_edges.
